# BITS

> BITS is a community for sharing, reusing and discovering small code snippets, with public profiles, groups, a language and dependency catalog, and a searchable command box.

## Product definition

BITS is a full-stack web product for sharing small, reusable code examples. It is designed around snippets rather than full repositories. Users can publish code with a primary language, optional dependencies, tags and a description, organise snippets into groups, and expose them through a public profile.

The public side of the product combines topic catalogs, search, author profiles and direct content links. Signed-in users can create, edit, copy, fork, favourite and delete their own content. Developers can create Website apps that support OAuth and API Keys, or Service apps that support API Keys only.

Chinese summary: BITS 是一个分享、复用和发现小型代码片段的社区，提供公开主页、代码分组、语言与依赖目录、搜索，以及 OAuth 与 API Key 开发者集成。

## Primary objects

- Snippet: a code example with one primary language, optional dependencies, up to five tags, a title, description, visibility and a code body.
- Group: a folder that organises related snippets. A snippet belongs to at most one group.
- Language: a public catalog entry used as the snippet's primary technology.
- Dependency: a framework, library, tool or runtime associated with one or more languages and selected snippets.
- User profile: the author's public page at `/{username}`, with avatar, nickname, bio, links, activity and visible content.
- Developer application: a Website app that can use OAuth and API Keys, or a Service app that can use API Keys only.
- OAuth service: credentials and configuration attached to one developer application.
- API Key: a scoped key attached to one application and one user account, with permissions, an optional expiry, a one-time secret and a last-used timestamp.

## How content works

- New snippets are created through a three-step flow: choose a language, select optional dependencies, then enter details and code.
- A snippet URL is initially generated from its display name. If the slug already exists for that account, a numeric suffix such as `-2` or `-3` is appended.
- A snippet or group slug can be renamed later. Supported old public detail, raw and edit links redirect to the new address.
- Titles, descriptions, language, dependencies, tags, group, visibility and code can also be edited.
- Deleting content hides it immediately. Deletion is soft, and site administrators can restore content.
- A copy is counted at most once per visitor, snippet and hour.
- Forking a public snippet opens a confirmation dialog where the current user can edit the new URL name and choose private, unlisted or public visibility before the copy is created. The copy retains a source link.
- A public group can be forked with its public snippets. Private snippets from the original group are not copied.

## Visibility and access

| Visibility | Who can open it | Search and indexing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Public | Everyone | Listed on profiles, catalog pages and public search |
| Unlisted | Anyone with the direct link | Excluded from search and marked noindex |
| Private | Only the owner | Never exposed on public pages |

Public and unlisted content require the author to set a username first. Visitors without permission receive a 404 rather than a separate access-denied page. A snippet uses its own visibility; a group page uses the group visibility and only lists snippets the visitor may open.

## Discovery and navigation

- `/languages` and `/dependencies` provide catalog entry points.
- `/language/{slug}` lists a language, related public snippets and relevant groups.
- `/{kind}/{slug}` lists dependencies where `kind` is `framework`, `library`, `tool` or `runtime`.
- `/search` returns public snippets and groups with pagination.
- Pressing `/` outside an input opens the command box. Supported commands include `/language`, `/framework`, `/lib`, `/tool`, `/runtime`, `/dep`, `/snippet`, `/group`, `/user`, `/new`, `/me`, `/favorites`, `/reports`, `/requests`, `/changelog`, `/go` and `/search`.
- Search separates multiple keywords with spaces. All keywords must match. Snippets are searched by title, description, tags, language and dependency names.

## Profiles and community

- A public profile lives at `/{username}` and displays avatar, nickname, bio, open links, content counts and public snippets and groups.
- The owner sees private and unlisted content plus additional management actions.
- Owner-only profile tabs cover favourites, reports and feedback, and catalog requests. These tabs are not public.
- Visitors can follow authors. The profile owner can manage followers and following from the follower dialogs.
- Owners can pin snippets and groups and reorder content.
- The contribution calendar publicly shows daily activity counts, not private content titles or feedback text.

## Developer platform

- [Developer platform](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/developer): Entry point for applications, OAuth services and API Keys.
- [Apps documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/apps): Application identity, Website versus Service app types, and how apps connect to OAuth services and API Keys.
- [OAuth documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/oauth): Endpoints, client authentication, scopes, authorization code flow, PKCE, refresh rotation, device flow, userinfo and revocation.
- [API Keys documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/api-keys): Creating scoped keys, selecting an owned app, permissions, expiry, one-time secret display, last use and revocation.
- [Open API v1 documentation](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/docs/developer/open-api): API-key authentication, snippet and group endpoints, pagination, errors, permissions and rate limits.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://bits.micropue.com.cn/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1.0 document for the `/api/v1` surface, versioned as API `1.0.0`.

### OAuth endpoints

- `GET /oauth/authorize`
- `POST /oauth/token`
- `GET /oauth/userinfo`
- `POST /oauth/revoke`
- `POST /oauth/device/code`
- `GET /oauth/device`

### OAuth facts

- Supported scopes: `read:user` and `read:email`.
- PKCE methods: `S256` and `plain`.
- Authorization codes are short-lived and single-use.
- Refresh tokens rotate; reuse of an old refresh token revokes the token family.
- The userinfo response includes `sub`, `username`, `nickname`, `avatar_url` and `profile`; `email` is included when authorised.
- Access tokens can expire, while an OAuth service can also be configured for a non-expiring token.

### API Keys and Open API

- Website apps can create API Keys and OAuth services; Service apps can create API Keys only.
- API Keys are shown in full once. Only a hash is stored; later views show a prefix, name, permissions, expiry, creation time and last-used time.
- Permissions are `content:read`, `content:create`, `content:update` and `content:delete`.
- Keys can expire after 30, 90 or 365 days, or never expire, and can be revoked immediately. A user can retain up to 50 active keys.
- `/api/v1` accepts an API Key through `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `X-API-Key`. Site cookies and OAuth access tokens are rejected.
- The Open API can read, create, update and soft-delete the key owner's snippets, and read, create, update and delete the owner's groups. It cannot change account profile, email, password, two-factor authentication, Passkeys, followers, favorites, OAuth grants or other security settings.
- Read requests are limited to 120 per minute per key; write requests are limited to 30 per minute per key. Open API rate limiting fails closed when its rate-limit store is unavailable.
- Open API endpoints:
  - `GET /api/v1/me`
  - `GET /api/v1/snippets`
  - `POST /api/v1/snippets`
  - `GET /api/v1/snippets/{slug}`
  - `PATCH /api/v1/snippets/{slug}`
  - `DELETE /api/v1/snippets/{slug}`
  - `GET /api/v1/groups`
  - `POST /api/v1/groups`
  - `GET /api/v1/groups/{slug}`
  - `PATCH /api/v1/groups/{slug}`
  - `DELETE /api/v1/groups/{slug}`

## Crawling guidance

- Use public content pages, documentation, catalogs and the sitemap.
- Do not treat private, deleted, account, developer-management or dashboard pages as public content.
- Unlisted content is reachable by direct link but should not be treated as search-indexed content.
- Prefer canonical URLs from the sitemap and use the displayed author username and content slug when citing a snippet.
- Use `/openapi.json` for the machine-readable definition of the authenticated Open API; it is not public content to crawl as a documentation page.

- Canonical site: https://bits.micropue.com.cn
- Product category: code snippet sharing and discovery community
- Supported developer protocols: OAuth 2.0 and API-Key-authenticated Open API v1
